findings.action: The audit skips a commit patch whenever git config --list is unchanged, but patch rendering also depends on mutable attributes. For example, changing .git/info/attributes to mark a changed text file -diff changes git show --binary output without changing the commit ID or effective configuration digest. This file is not captured by this stream path, so the final audit can certify stale patch bytes. The previous captured patch path reran this command. Audit all rendering dependencies or retain the streamed rerun until purity can be proved.

Concurrent first reads can both find no observation at line 143, release state.mu, and enter effectiveGitConfig. After one inserts its observation, the other's final insertion branch only adds its producer and never compares digest, length or error. Different streams can therefore both return success without making the producer unknown, violating R4. Compare results in this final existing-observation branch as well, or serialize observation initialization.

The configuration attached to an observation is obtained after the patch finishes and may also come from an earlier operation-local cached reading. It is not established as the configuration under which this patch was rendered. On a first read, Git can render under configuration A, configuration can change to B before effectiveGitConfig runs, and the observation is then tagged B. The final audit sees B and skips the A-rendered patch, even though the change persists. Bind configuration around the stream and refuse or rerun when that binding cannot be established.

The fresh configuration audit runs with item.ctx, which was stored using context.WithoutCancel and consequently has neither cancellation nor a deadline. The saved deadline is restored only later for the patch rerun. A blocked git config process, for example reading a configured include through a FIFO, can therefore hang final audit indefinitely despite the original read timeout. WaitDelay does not bound a still-running process. Apply the saved deadline or another explicit audit timeout to this configuration read.

R6 explicitly requires recording measured captured and streamed bytes for the successful pose-dist index run. The execution log records elapsed time, historical patch traffic and a statement that publication fits under 512 MiB, but gives neither measured captured bytes nor measured streamed bytes for the new operation. The integration check runs fixture tests rather than this corpus measurement. Record both counters with their operation boundaries and supporting measurement evidence before marking R6 satisfied.
